section.title: The ooSQLPackage Class
section.para: An ooSQLPackage object is an ooSQLite package that has been loaded: a shared library, written in C or C++, that describes the collations and functions it contains, and optionally a collation needed callback. Packages are loaded with the loadPackage method of the ooSQLExtensions class, which keeps them, and the package object is obtained with its getPackage method.

For many uses, the methods of the ooSQLExtensions class are enough: loadPackage can register the package on a connection, and autoPackage, autoFunction, autoCollation, and autoCollationNeeded make the package or its parts automatic. The package object is needed to register the package on a connection later, with register, or to register a single function or collation, perhaps under another name.

section.title: new (Class method)
section.para: An ooSQLPackage object can not be instantiated from Rexx code. Rather, the programmer uses the getPackage method of the ooSQLExtensions class to get a package object.

listitem.para: In general an external ooSQLite package is loaded through the loadPackage method of the ooSQLExtensions class. For many use cases, this may be sufficient. Some use cases, such as registering a single function from the package to a specific database connection, require the package object. The loaded package object can be obtained through the getPackage method.
Raises an error condition if invoked from Rexx code.

This example is from a program where only a single function in an ooSQLite package is needed to be registered with a database connection:
-- Load the package success = .ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage(packageFile) if \ success then do say 'Failed to load package' say ' Error code: ' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrCode say ' Error message:' .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrMsg
return .ooSQLExtensions~lastErrCode end
...
dbConn = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(dbName, .ooSQLite~OPEN_READWRITE)
-- Get the package and register a single function package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage')
function = package~getFunction('half') if function == .nil then do say 'Failed to get function: half' say ' Error code: ' package~lastErrCode say ' Error message:' package~lastErrMsg
return package~lastErrCode end
dbConn~createFunction('half', function)

section.title: lastErrCode (Attribute)
section.para: Reflects the result code of the last method invoked on the package.

listitem.para: A SQLite Result Code. It is 0, OK, if the last method succeeded.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.

The methods of the package set the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes, which are always updated together. The errors that a method reports are MISUSE: the package has no collation, function, or collation needed callback with that name. Some errors raise a syntax error instead.
The lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the ooSQLExtensions class are separate: they reflect the methods of that class.
See the example of getFunction.

section.title: lastErrMsg (Attribute)
section.para: Reflects the error message of the last method invoked on the package.

listitem.para: A message that explains the lastErrCode attribute, or no error if the last method succeeded.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.
See the remarks of lastErrCode.
See the example of getFunction.

section.title: getCollation
section.para: Returns a collation of the package, as an object that can be registered on a connection.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
name [required]
The name of the collation in the package. The case of the letters is significant.
An ooSQLCollation object, or .nil if the package has no collation with that name. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the package tell what went wrong.
autoCollation makes a collation of a package automatic, and register registers all the collations of the package at once.
The object is passed to the createCollation method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which registers the collation on the connection under the name given there. The same object is returned each time.

This example registers the ebcdic collation of the examplePackage package, which sorts as EBCDIC does: lowercase letters, then uppercase letters, then digits:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') say db~createCollation('ebcdic', package~getCollation('ebcdic')) sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('a'), ('A'), ('1'))" - "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE ebcdic;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['X'] end /* Output: 0 a A 1 */

section.title: getCollationNeeded
section.para: Returns the collation needed callback of the package, as an object that can be registered on a connection.

listitem.para: There are no arguments.
An ooSQLCollationNeeded object, or .nil if the package has no collation needed callback. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the package tell what went wrong.

A package has at most one collation needed callback. SQLite invokes it when a statement uses a collation that the connection does not have, so that it can register it. autoCollationNeeded makes it automatic.
The object is passed to the collationNeeded method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which also accepts the package itself. The same object is returned each time.

The testPackage package, which is built with the examples, has a collation needed callback that registers its collations when SQLite asks for them:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('testpackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('testPackage') say db~collationNeeded(package~getCollationNeeded) sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('a'), ('c'), ('b'))" - "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE reverseOrder;" rows = db~exec(sql, .true) do row over rows say row['X'] end /* Output: 0 c b a */

section.title: getFunction
section.para: Returns a function of the package, as an object that can be registered on a connection.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
name [required]
The name of the function in the package. The case of the letters is significant.
An ooSQLFunction object, or .nil if the package has no function with that name. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the package tell what went wrong.
autoFunction makes a function of a package automatic, and register registers all the functions of the package at once.

The object is passed to the createFunction method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which registers the function on the connection under the name given there, with the number of arguments of the package unless another one is given. The same object is returned each time.

This example registers the half function of the examplePackage package under another name, and then asks for a function that the package does not have:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') function = package~getFunction('half') say function say db~createFunction('mitad', function) sql = "SELECT mitad(price) AS m FROM foods WHERE name = 'Bacon';" say db~exec(sql, .true)[1]['M'] say package~getFunction('double') say package~lastErrMsg /* Output: an ooSQLFunction 0 1.875 The NIL object this package contains no function named double */

section.title: &changed11;register
section.para: Registers all that the package contains on a database connection.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
dbConn [required]
An open ooSQLiteConnection object.
Returns OK on success, or MISUSE if a part of the package could not be registered. On error, the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the package tell what went wrong.

The collation needed callback of the package, its collations, and its functions are registered in that order, with the names they have in the package; the method stops at the first that fails. The dbConn argument of loadPackage does the same when the package is loaded, and autoPackage does it on every new connection.
Raises an execution error, 98.900, if the connection is closed, and a syntax error, 88.900, if the argument is not an ooSQLiteConnection object.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a closed connection, or an object that is not a connection, crashed the interpreter.

This example registers the examplePackage package on an open connection:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') say package~register(db) sql = "SELECT strAggregate(name) AS s FROM foods WHERE type_id = 1;" say db~exec(sql, .true)[1]['S'] /* Output: 0 Bagels, Bagels, raisin */
